nodes.name: Breachstone
nodes.summary: Item combined from Breach splinters (5 types, one per Breachlord) to open the Breachlord's Domain via map device; Flawless variant added 3.16; removed with Breach rework in 3.28.

sources.locator: lead: splinters combine into a Breachstone to challenge the Breachlord

nodes.name: Elegant Hubris
nodes.summary: Eternal Empire Timeless Jewel (Legion 3.7.0) naming Cadiro, Victario and Caspiro (the last per wiki list of historical figures: Bust of Emperor Caspiro).

nodes.name: Glorious Vanity
nodes.summary: Vaal Timeless Jewel (Legion 3.7.0); its mods name Doryani ('bathed in the blood of ... sacrificed in the name of Doryani'); other variants name Xibaqua and Ahuatotli.

nodes.name: Horns of Kulamac
nodes.summary: Artifact guarded by the Order of the Djinn in the Forbidden Vaults, described by Jun as able to shift the energies of life freely; its origin is unknown even to Jun. Catarina, helped by Janus Perandus, took it; Jun believes it grants the Syndicate immortality (her belief only).

sources.locator: 20:19 horns of Kulamac; 21:41 theory they grant immortality

nodes.name: Timeless Jewel
nodes.summary: Jewels introduced in Legion league (3.7.0) that rewrite nearby passives by legion faction; variants include Glorious Vanity (Vaal: Doryani/Xibaqua/Ahuatotli) and Elegant Hubris (Eternal: Cadiro/Victario/Caspiro). Other jewels (Lethal Pride, Brutal Restraint, Militant Faith) exist but their figure lists were not verified.

nodes.name: Ahkeli, the Clayshaper
nodes.summary: Descendant of the primeval civilisation, 'Honoured Founder' of the Order of the Djinn who, with the surviving Maraketh, repelled Lightless invasions during the Winter of the World; central figure of late primeval history (Ahkeli's rings).

nodes.name: Ahuana
nodes.summary: Minimal node: Karui chieftain, daughter of Hyrri Ngamaku who succeeded her as ruler; encountered in the Halls of the Dead.

nodes.name: Ahuatotli, the Blind
nodes.summary: Vaal figure fought as a Delve boss in the Vaal Nexus (Grand Architect's Temple); also a Timeless Jewel (Glorious Vanity) name.

nodes.name: Ailith, First of the Keepers
nodes.summary: Founder/leader of the Keepers of the Flame (Order of the Purple Flame) in the Monastery; in PoE1 3.27/3.28 she enlists the Exile against the Hiveborn at the Coast (Act 6), gives the Exile the flame to burn Hiveborn barriers and destroys Fortified Breaches. Author of The Word of the Dreamer. Revealed (Keepers league) to have died long ago: the Dreamer preserved her essence and keeps copies of her, burning and replacing her when she learns this. Also in PoE2.

sources.locator: Talk to Ailith; summon Ailith to destroy Fortified Breach
written by Ailith, First of the Keepers
Dialogue "Enter Back Room": "you died, long ago. I preserved your essence."
Lore: Ailith founded the Order after visions; clone/preserved essence

nodes.name: Aisling Laffrey
nodes.summary: Syndicate member without established background. Immortal Syndicate member in Betrayal league (3.5.0).

nodes.name: Amanamu, Liege of the Lightless
nodes.summary: Abyssal Lich, commander of the Lightless and servant of Kulemak. Boss of the Abyssal Depths (Abyss league 3.1.0).

nodes.name: Aukuna, the Black Sekhema
nodes.summary: Sekhema (leader) of the Maraketh; general of the Maraketh legion.

nodes.name: Aul, the Crystal King
nodes.summary: Also Ahn; former slave who led an uprising and became the last king of the primeval civilisation; deceived by Kulemak (golem for power), which ended his civilisation; he sealed himself and his citadel in azurite crystal. Delve boss at depth 130+.

nodes.name: Cadiro Perandus
nodes.summary: Perandus family member and uncle of Emperor Chitus Perandus, who used his wealth to rig the Lord's Labyrinth in Chitus's favour. NPC of Perandus league (2.2.0) selling items for Perandus Coins from caches he hid after the Cataclysm; later available as Syndicate Research-safehouse/hideout NPC; named on the Elegant Hubris timeless jewel.

sources.locator: lead: Cadiro hid the family treasures in secret caches

nodes.name: Cameria the Coldblooded
nodes.summary: Assassin/murderer Syndicate member. Immortal Syndicate member in Betrayal league (3.5.0).

nodes.name: Catarina, Master of Undeath
nodes.summary: Necromancer forsaken master who became leader of the Immortal Syndicate (the Mastermind); wanted to become eternal queen; killed the Order of the Djinn for the Horns of Kulamac; boss in Mastermind's Lair. Writer of the Lifegiver's Manifesto.

nodes.name: Chitus Perandus
nodes.summary: Minimal node: Eternal Empire emperor of the Perandus family, nephew of Cadiro; assassinated during the Purity Rebellion by Ondar. Full entry owned by the Eternal Empire domain.

nodes.name: Craiceann, First of the Deep
nodes.summary: Spirit Beast avatar of the First Ones, First of the Deep ('First of All'), ancestor of crabs, squid and sea creatures; Bestiary encounter.

nodes.name: Dawn, Harbinger of Solaris
nodes.summary: Act 8 unique boss in the Solaris Temple Level 2 (quest Solar Eclipse). Per Maramoa 'the Dawn' was an exile who went insane and became a devotee of Solaris. Despite the title 'Harbinger' he is unrelated to Harbinger league.

nodes.name: Doryani, Queen's Thaumaturgist
nodes.summary: Minimal node (owned by Vaal domain): Vaal thaumaturgist under Atziri whose innovations and sacrifices contributed to the Fall of the Vaal; also appears in PoE2; named on Glorious Vanity.

nodes.name: Dusk, Harbinger of Lunaris
nodes.summary: Act 8 unique boss in the Lunaris Temple Level 2 (quest Lunar Eclipse). Per Maramoa 'the Dusk' is an exile-turned-sycophant who carried the Moon Orb into the Lunaris Temple. Unrelated to Harbinger league.

nodes.name: Einhar Frey
nodes.summary: Master-NPC beastmaster who teaches the Exile to capture beasts and runs the Menagerie; appears in Act 2 (Forest Encampment, Einhar's Hunt).

nodes.name: Elreon, Loremaster
nodes.summary: Exiled Templar who believed thaumaturgy a divine gift; forsaken master (jewellery). Immortal Syndicate member in Betrayal league (3.5.0).

nodes.name: Farrul, First of the Plains
nodes.summary: Spirit Beast avatar of the First Ones, First of the Plains ('First of the Hunt'), ancestor of hounds, cats and other mammals; Bestiary encounter.

nodes.name: Fenumus, First of the Night
nodes.summary: Spirit Beast avatar of the First Ones, First of the Night ('First Explorer'), ancestor of bugs and insectoids; Bestiary encounter.

nodes.name: Gravicius Reborn
nodes.summary: Former Act 3 general, resurrected Syndicate member. Immortal Syndicate member in Betrayal league (3.5.0).

nodes.name: Guff "Tiny" Grenn
nodes.summary: Syndicate member from the Brinerot warband. Immortal Syndicate member in Betrayal league (3.5.0).

nodes.name: Haku, Armourmaster
nodes.summary: Karui forsaken master (armour); Syndicate member. Immortal Syndicate member in Betrayal league (3.5.0).

nodes.name: Hillock
nodes.summary: First boss of Act 1 (Twilight Strand); exiled criminal turned zombie; later resurrected as Hillock, the Blacksmith of the Syndicate.

nodes.name: Hillock, the Blacksmith
nodes.summary: Act 1 boss Hillock resurrected by the Mastermind and joined the Syndicate. Immortal Syndicate member in Betrayal league (3.5.0).

nodes.name: Queen Hyrri Ngamaku
nodes.summary: Niece of King Kaom; trained in archery at Thebrus and led Karui women archers in the ambush that defeated Marceus Lioneye at Lioneye's Watch (Purity Rebellion). After Kaom's corruption she led 500 Karui families home to Ngamakanui, became queen, had a child with Victario, then vanished leading an army against an unknown threat; succeeded by Ahuana. General of the Karui legion in Legion league (3.7.0).

nodes.name: It That Fled
nodes.summary: Breach-realm creature that fled the Breachlords' rule and is listed among Immortal Syndicate members; most Syndicate members fear it. (Not in Keepers league.) Identity beyond that unclear.

sources.locator: 13:26 "being from the breach realm who fled the rule of the Breachlords"; 17:53 most members terrified of it
restrictions: It That Fled cannot appear in the Immortal Syndicate

nodes.name: It That Was Esh
nodes.summary: Hive Colony boss fought together with It That Was Tul (PoE1 3.27/3.28, PoE2 0.5.0). Per Ailith it is not the original Esh but possibly Esh's leftover remains after the fusion into Xesht.

nodes.name: It That Was Tul
nodes.summary: Hive Colony boss fought together with It That Was Esh (PoE1 3.27/3.28, PoE2 0.5.0); drops the Breachlord Sac / Breach rings. Per Ailith it is not the original Tul but possibly Tul's leftover remains after the fusion into Xesht.

nodes.name: Janus Perandus
nodes.summary: Great-grandson of Chitus Perandus; former Order of the Djinn member and gambling addict who betrayed the order to Catarina and joined the Syndicate.

nodes.name: Jun Ortoi
nodes.summary: Master NPC, survivor and guardian of the Forbidden Vaults of the Order of the Djinn; hunts the Syndicate after its killing of her order. Introduced in Betrayal; Act 9 quest "The Immortal Syndicate".

sources.locator: 1:05 Jun Ortoi, Order of the Djinn

nodes.name: Korell Goya
nodes.summary: Syndicate member from the Redblade warband. Immortal Syndicate member in Betrayal league (3.5.0).

nodes.name: Kulemak
nodes.summary: Creator and master of the Lightless and Lich Lords; exalted within the Well of Souls (power of necromancy); waged war on the surface, deceived Aul with a bargain for a stone golem, ending the primeval civilisation. Destroyed in mortal form by the Three Sisters; his soul returned to the Well. Appears in PoE2 (Rise of the Abyssal / Abyss).

nodes.name: Kurgal, the Blackblooded
nodes.summary: Abyssal Lich, commander of the Lightless and servant of Kulemak. Boss in the Lich's Tomb in Delve (depth 90+); born from a stone golem Kulemak created in his bargain with Aul.

nodes.name: Leo, Master of the Arena
nodes.summary: Pit master of the Sarn arena; forsaken master of PvP missions. Immortal Syndicate member in Betrayal league (3.5.0).

nodes.name: General Marceus Lioneye
nodes.summary: Eternal Empire general and leader of the Gemling Legion; archer with a virtue gem in one eye; defeated by Hyrri's ambush at Lioneye's Watch during the Purity Rebellion. (General of the Eternal Empire legion in Legion league, 3.7.0.)

nodes.name: Navali
nodes.summary: NPC seer of Prophecy league who sells prophecies for silver coins.

nodes.name: Niko the Mad
nodes.summary: Master-NPC miner who guides the Exile into the Azurite Mine; collects Voltaxic Sulphite to power his Crawler (a repurposed Eternal torture device) and generator.

nodes.name: Rigwald, the Wolven King
nodes.summary: Ezomyte thane of Ezomyr who received Victario's letters seeking aid for the Purity Rebellion; possessed by the Greatwolf during the Rebellion. Boss of the Talisman league; his memoirs are the Inscription lore found at Stone Altars. NOT a member of the Immortal Syndicate (the Betrayal video only notes Thane Jorgin shares the title 'thane' with him).

sources.locator: Rigwald, the Wolven King: boss of the Talisman league
The Greatwolf: Rigwald possessed during the Purity Rebellion
Victario wrote letters to Thane Rigwald of Ezomyr

nodes.name: Riker Maloney
nodes.summary: Syndicate member without established background. Immortal Syndicate member in Betrayal league (3.5.0).

nodes.name: Rin Yuushu
nodes.summary: Syndicate member from the Mutewind warband. Immortal Syndicate member in Betrayal league (3.5.0).

nodes.name: Cardinal Sanctus Vox
nodes.summary: Oriathan noble, ancestor of the Vox family; general of the Templar legion.

nodes.name: Saqawal, First of the Sky
nodes.summary: Spirit Beast avatar of the First Ones, First of the Sky ('Last of the First'), ancestor of birds and reptiles; Bestiary encounter.

nodes.name: Tecrod
nodes.summary: 'The Hated Slave': Abyssal Lich Lord who, unlike Amanamu, Kurgal and Ulaman, acts independently of Kulemak (PoE1 wiki: forsaken by Kulemak for unclear reasons). In PoE2 (Legacy of the Precursors) he steals the Flame Seed on his wyrm, seeks Kulemak's favour, hunts for the Edicts and is destroyed by the Arbiter of Divinity.

sources.locator: Lore: independent of Kulemak; steals Flame Seed; destroyed by Arbiter of Divinity

nodes.name: Thane Jorgin
nodes.summary: Syndicate member (Betrayal, 3.5.0) who left as a mere after being accused of killing his brother; believes Rin or another Brotherhood of Silence member responsible (per video). Video notes he shares the title 'thane' with Rigwald; Jun mocks his 'first ones' (Ezomyte) background.

nodes.name: The Dreamer
nodes.summary: Keepers-league NPC (full name: Chayula, the Benevolent Dreamer / the One Who Dreamt) found hidden in the Monastery of the Keepers. After the failed fusion of the five Breachlords he was torn asunder and cast into the void; he gave Ailith visions and the Genesis Tree as weapon against the Hiveborn, calls the Exile an ally 'for now', and destroys Ailith's body when she learns the truth (she is a preserved Hiveborn copy).

sources.locator: Dialogue ("Who are you?", "Who is our enemy?", Enter Back Room) and Lore
Visions V: the Four have become One; Genesis Tree is his gift
Lore: Chayula spoke to humans through dreams, founding the Keepers

nodes.name: The Trialmaster
nodes.summary: Minimal node (owned by PoE2 domain): per the Order of the Djinn page, the Trialmaster is the former Order member Ixchel, 'Godstealer'.

nodes.name: Tora, Master of the Hunt
nodes.summary: Forsaken master (ranged weapons); studied corruption in beasts. Immortal Syndicate member in Betrayal league (3.5.0).

nodes.name: Ulaman, Sovereign of the Well
nodes.summary: Abyssal Lich, commander of the Lightless and servant of Kulemak. Boss of the Abyssal Depths (Abyss league 3.1.0).

nodes.name: Vagan, Weaponmaster
nodes.summary: Duelist forsaken master (weapons). Immortal Syndicate member in Betrayal league (3.5.0).

nodes.name: Victario Nevalius, the People's Poet
nodes.summary: Sarn poet and key supporter of the Purity Rebellion who incited Sarn against Emperor Chitus and Malachai; wrote to Thane Rigwald seeking Ezomyte aid; killed in Sarn during the Cataclysm. Named on the Elegant Hubris timeless jewel; father of Hyrri Ngamaku's child per wiki.

nodes.name: Viper Napuatzi
nodes.summary: General of the Vaal legion in the Timeless Conflict. (General of the Vaal legion in Legion league, 3.7.0.)

nodes.name: Vorici, Master Assassin
nodes.summary: Forsaken master (socket/colour crafting); Brotherhood of Silence member. Immortal Syndicate member in Betrayal league (3.5.0).

nodes.name: Vruun, Marshal of Xesht
nodes.summary: PoE2 boss in Unstable Breaches, marshal serving Xesht; drops Lineage supports.

sources.locator: Version History: introduced in 0.5.0; boss in Unstable Breaches

nodes.name: Xesht-Ula, the Open Hand
nodes.summary: Unique Breach monster (Atlas notable Call of Xesht-Ula, 3.17.0; no longer encounterable since 3.28.0) whose name is a portmanteau of the five Breachlords; summons apparitions of each lord and can drop any breachstone. The PoE2 wiki says the Breachlords had planned to merge into a being called Xesht-Ula. Not the same entity as Xesht.

sources.locator: Lore: Vaal Cult of the Purple Flame knew of the five Breachlords' plan to merge into Xesht-Ula

nodes.name: Xibaqua
nodes.summary: Historical figure of the Vaal Empire whose remains were believed to be the original progenitor of all Vaal; born from flesh of ancient Vaal gods; named on a Glorious Vanity variant.

nodes.name: Zana, Master Cartographer
nodes.summary: Forsaken master (Master Cartographer) who survives Betrayal. The wiki has a separate page for Zana Caeserius 'the Originator' of Secrets of the Atlas; the Master page is linked as 'the former Master', implying the same person, but the identity is not spelled out here. Owned by another domain.

nodes.name: The Abyss
nodes.summary: Cracks and pits that spawn monsters when approached; source of abyss jewels, Stygian Vises and the Abyssal Depths in PoE1 Abyss league (3.1.0); PoE2 Rise of the Abyssal (0.3.0) revives Abysses with the Well of Souls and desecration.

nodes.name: Azurite
nodes.summary: Crystal mined in Delve and spent for supplies; also the material in which Aul encased his citadel.

nodes.name: The Beyond
nodes.summary: Plane of demons reachable via Beyond portals in Beyond league (1.2.0); Beyond demons later became a core mechanic (Beyond passives replaced Breach ones in Keepers league).

sources.locator: restrictions: Beyond passives moved to take Breach's place

nodes.name: The Breach
nodes.summary: Otherworldly realm/phenomenon whose tears let Breach monsters enter Wraeclast; original Breach league (2.5.0) had breaches expanding as monsters are killed, splinters forming Breachstones for the five Breachlords' Domains. Replaced in 3.28.0 by the Keepers-of-the-Flame rework (Hiveborn, Ailith, Genesis Tree). PoE2 has Unstable Breaches and the Breachlords' lore (Xesht).

sources.locator: version history 3.28.0: new Breach replaces original Breach mechanic

nodes.name: Darkness (Delve)
nodes.summary: Lightless darkness in the Azurite Mine that damages unprepared delvers; requires flares; Aul and Kurgal fights include a darkness phase.

nodes.name: Essence
nodes.summary: Imprisoned essences freed in Essence league (2.4.0, Atlas of Worlds); modify items with guaranteed affixes; can be corrupted (Hysteria, Delirium, Horror, Insanity).

nodes.name: Forsaken Masters
nodes.summary: Seven NPC masters introduced in Forsaken Masters (1.2.0): Elreon, Haku, Vorici, Vagan, Tora, Leo and Catarina (plus Zana); they vanished at Betrayal, taken by the Syndicate (all but Zana).

nodes.name: The Genesis Tree
nodes.summary: Tree in the Monastery that consumes Graftblood and births rewards (wombgifts); Exile bonds with it to complete Into the Breach.

sources.locator: Allocate a Womb; Quest Complete bonded with the Genesis Tree

nodes.name: Harbinger
nodes.summary: Otherworldly enemies of Harbinger league (3.0.0) beaten by killing their minions; drop currency shards.

nodes.name: Prophecy
nodes.summary: Prophecy system of Prophecy league (2.3.0); removed in 3.17.0; Pale Council bosses.

nodes.name: The Red Pyre
nodes.summary: Entity/title in Ailith's Word of the Dreamer ('The Red Pyre burns hot... The Dreamer once knew him, before his addiction'). The fire imagery and the book's subject (the four Breachlords that became Xesht) point to Xoph, Dark Embers; the identification is inferred, not stated.

nodes.name: Rogue exiles
nodes.summary: Exiled criminals who roam Wraeclast as hostile NPCs; originated in Anarchy league (0.11.0), later reused in PoE2 (Lichborn exiles in Rise of the Abyssal).

sources.locator: raising a rogue exile as Lichborn

nodes.name: Timeless Conflict
nodes.summary: Legions of different factions (Karui, Maraketh, Templar, Eternal Empire, Vaal) frozen in stasis by a timeless monolith, locked in an endless battle; broken out of stasis by damaging them. Why they are frozen is not explained in the wiki.

nodes.name: Tormented spirits
nodes.summary: Spirits of tormented criminals in Torment league (1.3.0) that flee, empower nearby monsters and drop loot; unrelated to Kitava's Torments in Act 5.

nodes.name: Hiveborn
nodes.summary: Breach monsters invading Wraeclast in the reworked Breach; fought by the Exile and Ailith, source of Graftblood and Hiveblood.

nodes.name: Chayula, Who Dreamt
nodes.summary: One of five Breachlords (chaos). Boss of Chayula's Domain (male per wiki). As the Dreamer (Keepers league) he opposes the Xesht fusion. Original Breach bosses introduced in 2.5.0 (Chayula to the core game 2.6.0 per wiki version history), removed 3.28.0.

sources.locator: Lore: the Dreamer is Chayula, a Breachlord

nodes.name: Esh, Forked Thought
nodes.summary: One of five Breachlords. Lightning damage Breachlord. Boss residing in Esh's Domain; Breachstone/Flawless Breachstone via map device (PoE1 2.5.0; domains removed 3.28.0).

nodes.name: The Greatwolf
nodes.summary: First Ones-type god of the hunt and ancestor of wolves and werewolves; possessed Rigwald, the Wolven King, during the Purity Rebellion.

nodes.name: Lunaris
nodes.summary: Minimal node (owned elsewhere): Sun/Moon deity of the Eternal/Templar pantheon.

nodes.name: Solaris
nodes.summary: Minimal node (owned elsewhere): Sun/Moon deity of the Eternal/Templar pantheon.

nodes.name: Tul, Creeping Avalanche
nodes.summary: One of five Breachlords. Cold Breachlord (female per wiki). Boss residing in Tul's Domain; Breachstone/Flawless Breachstone via map device (PoE1 2.5.0; domains removed 3.28.0).

nodes.name: Uul-Netol, Unburdened Flesh
nodes.summary: One of five Breachlords. Physical damage Breachlord. Boss residing in Uul-Netol's Domain; Breachstone/Flawless Breachstone via map device (PoE1 2.5.0; domains removed 3.28.0).

nodes.name: Xesht, We Who Are One
nodes.summary: Entity of the Breach (PoE2 wiki: Xesht): the incomplete fusion of four Breachlords (Xoph, Esh, Tul, Uul-Netol) after the planned five-way merger failed; Chayula was severed from the union and opposes it as the Dreamer. Per the Dreamer, Xesht is 'four minds sewn together' filled with endless rage and hunger.

sources.locator: Trivia: Xesht is the incomplete fusion of Xoph, Esh, Tul, Uul-Netol; Chayula opposes as the Dreamer
Dialogue "Who is our enemy?": "Xoph... Esh... Tul... Uul-Netol... our melding... failed... They became Xesht."
Lore: failed merge of the five Breachlords; Chayula severed, rest formed Xesht

nodes.name: Xoph, Dark Embers
nodes.summary: One of five Breachlords (fire). Boss of Xoph's Domain, accessed via Xoph's Breachstone in a map device (2.5.0; removed from game 3.28.0). Model based on a Marauder; one of four lords fused into Xesht.

nodes.name: Winter of the World
nodes.summary: Initial Abyssal (Lightless) invasion of the surface, ended by the Three Sisters who destroyed Kulemak's mortal form and brought back the sun. Minimal node; fuller entry owned by another domain.

nodes.name: The Immortal Syndicate
nodes.summary: Group of resurrected criminals and the missing forsaken masters under Catarina (the Mastermind), with 17 other members in four divisions (Transportation, Fortification, Research, Intervention); aims to become the ruling power in Wraeclast. Jun believes (not confirmed) the Horns of Kulamac give them their return-from-death ability.

nodes.name: Keepers of the Flame (Order of the Purple Flame)
nodes.summary: Monastic order founded by Ailith after her visions of the Dreamer; they train in the Monastery to defend Wraeclast against the Hiveborn and tend the Genesis Tree. The PoE2 wiki calls it the Order of the Purple Flame; the Monk class belongs to it. It is a taboo among them to speak the Dreamer's true name (Chayula).

sources.locator: Visit the Monastery of the Keepers: "Welcome to our Monastery..."

nodes.name: The Lightless
nodes.summary: Necromantic army of possessed golems created by Kulemak, led by Abyssal Liches; ended the primeval civilisation.

nodes.name: Order of the Djinn
nodes.summary: Secret society founded in ancient times by the Maraketh and the Clayshaper (Ahkeli) that protects Wraeclast from calamity and guards dangerous artefacts (Forbidden Vaults near the Oasis, Act 9); takes one orphan from each culture. Members forged and delivered the Starforge to the Watchers of Decay (video). Janus Perandus's betrayal let Catarina raid the vault and the Order was slain except Jun and Janus; in PoE2 Jun is rebuilding it. Past members include Ixchel (later the Trialmaster).

sources.locator: 1:07 order of the Djinn; 16:34 Starforge; 20:10 infiltration of Forbidden Vault

nodes.name: Perandus family
nodes.summary: Wealthy and powerful Eternal Empire family that put Malachai in place; basis for the Perandus league treasures.

nodes.name: Primeval Civilization ("Proto-Vaal")
nodes.summary: Ancient civilisation preceding the Vaal, unearthed in the Azurite Mine; the name "Proto-Vaal" is an internal term never used in-game and no link to the Vaal is established.

nodes.name: The First Ones
nodes.summary: Animalistic gods worshipped by the Ezomytes, believed to roam the realm of Spirit; their avatars are Spirit Beasts: Saqawal (birds/reptiles, 'Last of the First'), Farrul (hounds/cats/mammals, 'First of the Hunt'), Fenumus (insects, 'First Explorer'), Craiceann (crabs/squid/sea life, 'First of All'). Also The Greatwolf and the Gull.

sources.locator: Craiceann section: avatar of the First Ones

nodes.name: The Three Sisters
nodes.summary: Sun, Moon (and Earth) sisters/gods named differently per culture who ended the Winter of the World by destroying Kulemak's mortal form. Minimal node; owned by another domain.

nodes.name: Warbands (Redblade, Brinerot, Mutewind)
nodes.summary: Three roaming warring clans of Warbands league (2.0.0) with leaders and elites: Redblade, Brinerot, Mutewind; members Korell Goya, Guff Grenn, Rin Yuushu later joined the Syndicate.

nodes.name: Abyss league
nodes.summary: Abyss league Launched 2017-12-08 (version 3.1.0). Abysses are cracks and pits spawning monsters; introduces abyss jewels, Stygian Vises, Abyssal Depths and Abyssal Liches.

nodes.name: Ambush league
nodes.summary: Ambush league launched 2014-03-05 (1.1.0, Sacrifice of the Vaal); introduced Strongboxes. Ran with hardcore Invasion league.

nodes.name: Anarchy league
nodes.summary: Anarchy league launched 2013-06-07 (0.11.0); introduced rogue exiles and league challenges. Hardcore twin: Onslaught.

nodes.name: Bestiary league
nodes.summary: Bestiary league Launched 2018-03-02 (version 3.2.0). Einhar Frey teaches the Exile to capture beasts with nets, for beastcrafting and to challenge the Spirit Beasts (the First Ones).

nodes.name: Betrayal league
nodes.summary: Betrayal league Launched 2018-12-07 (version 3.5.0). Jun Ortoi leads the hunt for the Immortal Syndicate, which has taken the forsaken masters; revamps the master system.

nodes.name: Beyond league
nodes.summary: Beyond league launched 2014-08-20 (1.2.0, Forsaken Masters): extradimensional demons invade via portals that grow with nearby kills, culminating in a unique boss. Hardcore twin of Rampage.

nodes.name: Bloodlines league
nodes.summary: Bloodlines league Launched 2014-12-13 (version 1.3.0). Hardcore twin of Torment; Bloodline-empowered monsters with special modifiers. (Mechanic detail abbreviated; release data from wiki.)

nodes.name: Breach league
nodes.summary: Breach league Launched 2016-12-02 (version 2.5.0). Breaches open parallel realms of otherworldly monsters; splinters form Breachstones to challenge the five Breachlords in their domains.

nodes.name: Delve league
nodes.summary: Delve league Launched 2018-08-31 (version 3.4.0). Niko the Mad guides the Exile into the infinite Azurite Mine beneath Wraeclast, powered by Voltaxic Sulphite.

nodes.name: Domination league
nodes.summary: Domination league launched 2013-10-23 (1.0.0, Path of Exile release); introduced Shrines. Hardcore twin: Nemesis.

nodes.name: Essence league
nodes.summary: Essence league launched 2016-09-02 (2.4.0, Atlas of Worlds): frozen monsters hold an Essence; freeing them grants it. Essences give guaranteed affixes and can be corrupted.

nodes.name: Harbinger league
nodes.summary: Harbinger league launched 2017-08-04 (3.0.0, The Fall of Oriath): otherworldly Harbingers, defeated by destroying their minions, drop shards of currency.

nodes.name: Invasion league
nodes.summary: Invasion league Launched 2014-03-05 (version 1.1.0). Hardcore twin of Ambush; invasion bosses spawn in areas. (Mechanic detail abbreviated; release data from wiki.)

nodes.name: Keepers of the Flame league
nodes.summary: PoE1 league (3.27.0) that introduced the new Breach (Hiveborn, Ailith, Genesis Tree); the mechanic became core in 3.28.0 replacing the original Breach. Minimal node; full release data owned by another domain.

sources.locator: lead; Into the Breach version history

nodes.name: Legion league
nodes.summary: Legion league Launched 2019-06-07 (version 3.7.0). Timeless Monoliths reveal legions frozen mid-battle; Emblems open the Domain of Timeless Conflict. Legion mechanic reworked in 3.29 per wiki (incubators no longer drop).

nodes.name: Nemesis league
nodes.summary: Nemesis league launched 2013-10-23 (1.0.0); every rare monster has a Nemesis modifier. Standard twin: Domination.

nodes.name: Onslaught league
nodes.summary: Onslaught league launched 2013-06-07 (0.11.0); monsters have 20% increased movement and attack speed. Standard twin: Anarchy.

nodes.name: Perandus league
nodes.summary: Perandus league launched 2016-03-04 (2.2.0, Ascendancy): after the Cataclysm Cadiro Perandus hid family treasures in caches across Wraeclast; players open guarded caches and trade Perandus Coins with Cadiro.

nodes.name: Rise of the Abyssal league (PoE2)
nodes.summary: First PoE2 full league, launched 2025-08-29 with version 0.3.0 (The Third Edict); Abysses, preserved bones, the Well of Souls (Act 2) and desecrated modifiers.

nodes.name: Prophecy league
nodes.summary: Prophecy league launched 2016-06-03 (2.3.0): silver coins traded with Navali for prophecies; the Pale Council league bosses of the Pale Court were tied to prophecies.

nodes.name: Rampage league
nodes.summary: Rampage league Launched 2014-08-20 (version 1.2.0). Kill-streak mechanic (paired with Beyond), part of Forsaken Masters. (Mechanic detail abbreviated; release data from wiki.)

nodes.name: Talisman league
nodes.summary: Talisman league launched 2015-12-11 (version 2.1.0). Monsters are possessed by ancient Ezomyte Talismans; killing them yields the Talisman. Boss: Rigwald, the Wolven King.

nodes.name: Tempest league
nodes.summary: Tempest league launched 2015-07-10 (2.0.0, The Awakening); hardcore sibling of Warbands that introduced Tempests, area modifiers that alter monsters and players (size, damage, drops).

nodes.name: Torment league
nodes.summary: Torment league launched 2014-12-13 (1.3.0): spirits of tormented criminals haunt areas, flee when met, imbue monsters and yield their ill-gotten gains when slain. Hardcore twin: Bloodlines.

nodes.name: Warbands league
nodes.summary: Warbands league Launched 2015-07-10 (version 2.0.0). Warring clans (Redblade, Brinerot, Mutewind) roam Wraeclast in synergistic groups with leaders and elites. (Mechanic detail abbreviated; release data from wiki.)

nodes.name: Abyssal Depths

nodes.name: The Crystal King's Throne

nodes.name: The Word of the Dreamer
nodes.summary: Environmental-lore book in the Monastery of the Keepers written by Ailith recording five visions of the Dreamer. Four visions warn of the Mother (births flesh), the Red Pyre (flame/addiction), the Forked Psyche (thought without will) and the Preserved Patterns (imprisoned bodies), each of whom the Dreamer 'once knew'; the fifth says the Four have become One and that the Genesis Tree is his gift. The mapping of these four to Uul-Netol (flesh), Xoph (fire), Esh (forked thought) and Tul (preserved/frozen) is inference from epithets and the wiki's note that the book is about the four Breachlords that became Xesht.
